part2.question: An environmental law you would like your country to introduce

segments.v: I want to talk about a law to stop burning rice straw and rubbish. In Vietnam, after the harvest, many farmers burn straw in their fields. Some families also burn rubbish. The smoke goes to Hà Nội and the air becomes very bad. I think the government should ban this. People who burn straw must pay a fine. The government should also help farmers use straw in other ways, like growing mushrooms. People should follow this law because smoke is bad for our health. I think people in the city will like this law but farmers may not like it at first. I think this law is very important for clean air.

fluency.band6: Clear, with modal verbs, but general.
fluency.band9: The law → the problem (cause and effect on Hà Nội) → how the law would work (second conditional) → why people should follow it → honest view on popularity → personal link → conclusion.

lexical.band6: burn, smoke, ban, fine, bad for health, important.
lexical.band9: in the open, backed up by, harvest, leftover, drifts, visibility, repeat offenders, on its own, animal feed, fine particles, political will.

grammar.band9: Consistent second conditional (would be banned; wouldn't work; could actually earn), relative clause (fines that increase for repeat offenders), and indirect clause (how thick the smoke can get).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 is clear, with modal verbs (should, must), but general. Band 9 explains the cause and effect of the problem, designs the law in detail using the second conditional, anticipates resistance, and explains why support matters.
